title: Liverpool’s Christian Benteke close to Crystal Palace move after talks resume
trail: Crystal Palace have resumed negotiations with Liverpool over the transfer of Christian Benteke, with the Belgium striker close to completing the move
body: Crystal Palace have resumed negotiations with Liverpool over the transfer of Christian Benteke, with the Belgium striker close to completing his move to Selhurst Park for a club record fee. Palace, who rejected an £18m bid from Everton for the forward Yannick Bolasie this week, have been in the market for a target man all summer after signing Andros Townsend from Newcastle in June. They agreed a fee with Marseille for Michy Batshuayi before he opted to join Chelsea and subsequently had two offers for Benteke rejected by Liverpool. The second, worth up to £30m with add-ons, fell short of Liverpool’s valuation of a player purchased from Aston Villa last summer for £32.5m. But after Jürgen Klopp warned potential suitors that he would not allow Benteke to be a “present” last week, Palace have reopened talks in the hope of concluding a transfer before the start of the Premier League season. It is understood that the 25-year-old is standing by to have a medical once a fee – with the potential to be worth around £32m including add-ons and bonuses – has been agreed. Palace have agreed to match Benteke’s £120,000-a-week wages, which would make him the club’s highest-paid player. His agent, Eris Kismet, told the Guardian on Sunday that he was hopeful his client’s future could be resolved soon. Benteke was signed by Brendan Rodgers from Villa and scored nine Premier League goals in his first season. However, Klopp made it clear that the striker is no longer part of his plans before Saturday’s friendly victory against Barcelona. “Christian already said it maybe makes sense for him to go to another club and that’s the situation at this moment,” he said. “Christian is still a great striker and that’s how it is, but we have a few more strikers and in this moment it makes more sense to give them match time and that is what we did. “If there are clubs that want a striker from us they have to make real offers and are not hoping for anything else, otherwise we will find solutions. “If there is a need on the other side then go for it – but not as a present. That’s how transfers are. A few clubs try to gamble but we are not part of the gambling side. We are serious people, and if there is an offer we will think about it.”
